summary: Microsoft Azure Virtual Machineのライフサイクルポリシーでは、General Purpose、Memory Optimized、Compute Optimized、Storage Optimizedの各VMファミリーを対象に、Current、Extended、End of Life、Retiredの4段階を明確化した。各段階ごとに新規導入可否、サポート、リージョンやクォータ、購入オプションと価格の扱いを定義し、移行計画を立てやすくする。End of Lifeでは通知や移行ツールを提供し、Retiredでは新規作成不可かつ既存VMも割り当て解除される。
keyPoints: このポリシーの初回対象はGeneral Purpose、Memory Optimized、Compute Optimized、Storage Optimizedの4系統で、まずこれらのVMファミリーに適用される。
Currentは新規導入向けとして推奨され、広いリージョンで一般提供される。Extendedも既存ワークロード向けに引き続きサポートされるが、Current段階への移行検討開始が求められ、クォータ制限の対象になり得る。
End of Lifeは退役が正式発表された段階で、新規デプロイやクォータ要求は制限対象になる一方、既存利用者には通知、移行ツール、ガイダンスが提供される。価格や提供条件の変更も想定される。
RetiredになるとVMは新規作成できず、既存VMも割り当て解除される。SLAとMicrosoftサポートの対象外となり、購入もできない。
significance: Azureで対象VM群を運用する利用者にとって、どの段階で新規展開、継続運用、移行、退役対応が必要かを共通の基準で判断しやすくなる。特に旧世代VMの利用者は、End of Life以降の配備制限やRetired時の停止条件を事前に把握でき、Azure AdvisorやService Healthで影響資産と推奨アクションを追跡できる。
summaryEn: Microsoft Azure Virtual Machine has clarified a four-stage lifecycle policy—Current, Extended, End of Life, and Retired—for its General Purpose, Memory Optimized, Compute Optimized, and Storage Optimized VM families. For each stage, it defines deployment eligibility, support, regional and quota behavior, and purchasing and pricing treatment to make transition planning easier. In End of Life, Azure provides notifications and migration tools, while in Retired, new creation stops and existing VMs are deallocated.
keyPointsEn: The initial scope of the policy is four VM categories: General Purpose, Memory Optimized, Compute Optimized, and Storage Optimized.

Current is recommended for new deployments and is broadly generally available across regions. Extended remains supported for existing workloads, but customers are expected to start planning a move to Current-stage VMs, and quota restrictions may apply.

End of Life begins when retirement is formally announced. New deployments and quota requests become subject to restriction, while existing customers receive notifications, migration tooling, and guidance. Changes to pricing and availability are also expected.
Once a VM series is Retired, it can no longer be newly provisioned and existing VMs will be deallocated. It also loses SLA and Microsoft support eligibility and is no longer available for purchase.
significanceEn: For customers operating the covered Azure VM families, the policy makes it easier to judge under a common framework when to deploy new workloads, continue operations, migrate, or complete retirement work. Users of older-generation VMs are especially affected because they can see deployment restrictions that start in End of Life and the shutdown conditions in Retired ahead of time, while Azure Advisor and Service Health help track impacted resources and recommended actions.
